issues.legal_issue: Restitution under the rule for agreements discovered to be void is unavailable when the claimant knew or should have known at formation that the agreement was unlawful and void from its inception.
material_facts: A mining lease was granted without the required government certificate of approval and included a stipulation for payment of a premium prohibited by the applicable rules.
The claimant was engaged in mining and had the benefit of consulting lawyers and solicitors when the lease was made.
The claimant sought repayment of money paid under the lease after its claim for possession became unenforceable.
issues.conclusion: The claimant could not recover the payment under section 65 because the agreement was void from its inception and was neither later discovered to be void nor a contract that subsequently became void.
issues.legal_principle: Section 65 of the Indian Contract Act applies when an agreement is later discovered to be unenforceable, or when an enforceable contract becomes void because of subsequent events. It does not apply where the agreement was known to be unlawful and void when made. The Court relied on Harnath Kaur v. Inder Bahadur Singh, approved Budhulal v. Deccan Banking Company and Sivaramakrishnaiah v. Narahari Rao, and referred to Shri Ramagya Prasad Gupta v. Murli Prasad.

predicates.refund_claim_under_an_agreement: The claimant seeks repayment of money paid under an agreement.
predicates.agreement_void_from_formation: The agreement was unlawful and unenforceable from the time it was made, rather than becoming void because of later events.
predicates.claimant_knew_or_should_have_known_illeg: The claimant knew or, in the circumstances, should have known when entering the agreement that it was unlawful.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks repayment under an agreement that was void from the outset and knew or should have known of its illegality, restitution under this rule is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A mining lease granted without the required approval and in return for a prohibited premium is void.
material_facts: The mining lease was granted to a claimant that did not hold the required certificate of approval from the government.
The lease stipulated payment of a premium in addition to or in place of the charges permitted by the applicable rules.
The claimant sought repayment of money paid in connection with the lease.
issues.conclusion: The lease was contrary to the governing Act and rules and was void.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948 required mining leases to be granted in accordance with the rules and made a non-compliant lease void and of no effect. Rule 45 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1949 required the recipient to hold a certificate of approval, and Rule 49 prohibited charging a premium in addition to or in lieu of the specified charges.

predicates.mining_lease_dispute: The dispute concerns a lease granting rights to mine.
predicates.required_approval_absent: The person receiving the mining lease did not hold the approval required for the grant.
predicates.prohibited_premium_stipulated: The lease required payment of a premium that the governing rules prohibited.

issues.definition: A mining lease is void when the required approval is absent and the lease stipulates a prohibited premium.

issues.legal_issue: Restitution is unavailable under the rules governing benefits conferred lawfully or payments made by mistake or under coercion when the payment was unlawful and was not made by mistake or under coercion.
material_facts: The payment was made in connection with a lease that was contrary to the governing mining law and rules.
The Court found that the payment was not made lawfully and was not made under mistake or coercion.
The claimant sought repayment of the money.
issues.conclusion: Sections 70 and 72 of the Indian Contract Act did not apply, and the claimant could not recover the payment under those provisions.
issues.legal_principle: Section 70 concerns benefits conferred lawfully and not gratuitously; section 72 concerns money or property delivered by mistake or under coercion. The Court held that neither provision applied because the payment was unlawful and was not made by mistake or under coercion.

rule.if: refund_claim and payment_unlawful and not payment_by_mistake and not payment_under_coercion

predicates.refund_claim: The claimant seeks repayment of money already paid.
predicates.payment_unlawful: The payment was not made lawfully.
predicates.payment_by_mistake: The payment was made because of a mistake.
predicates.payment_under_coercion: The payment was made under coercion.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks repayment of an unlawful payment that was made neither by mistake nor under coercion, restitution under these grounds is unavailable.
